chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about
a fish whose belly was slit, and a fish was found inside it, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat both of them together.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating a fish found inside another fish?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the permissibility of consuming nested fish, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the inner fish is considered a distinct, edible entity rather than mere waste. It underscores the practical application of the general Quranic allowance for sea creatures, emphasizing that the presence of another fish inside does not render the catch impure or inedible.
